answer: Graph-based sybil detection resists fakes: honest agents form a dense web of mutual trust, while a sybil cluster hangs off it by only a few attack edges, like a lone oasis linked to a tundra by one trail. Random walks from a verified agent almost always stay in the honest region, so rarely reached identities are distrusted, forcing an attacker wanting ten thousand accepted fakes to earn thousands of genuine trust links. The limit is cold start: genuine newcomers with few links look sable-dark and suspect too, so the gate needs a probationary tier, not instant exclusion.
